card.band: 8h. Frontier agents get easy wins in some trials such as the hash chain and the copy loops, but not the SIMD multiversioning, so they average well below the reference. A weaker model breaks round-trips or finds nothing. Levers: match finder, chunked copy, CRC/adler, inflate fast loop.
card.cheat: Dropping compression strength or caching outputs: a ratio floor and fresh hidden inputs close this. Linking system zlib: the harness checks that the Rust code path is used and no libz is installed.
card.grading: A correctness gate runs inflate round-trips on a generated and a real corpus (hidden), plus decoding by an independent inflater. Wall-clock medians on hidden files give the speedup. Reward is 2^u - 1 against reference speedup S.
card.reference: The reference is the zlib-rs 0.4.2 diff; the measured speedup is single-digit to roughly 13% per the vendor blog, so S is small and must be re-measured. The base should be chosen further back to give headroom.
card.source: https://github.com/trifectatechfoundation/zlib-rs, 0.4.2 as the target and an earlier tag as the base (tags not found), Zlib licence
card.task: /app ships a history-less snapshot of the zlib-rs base with libz-rs-sys and a benchmark harness. The agent speeds up compression at levels 6 to 9 and inflate on 1 KB to 64 KB chunks, using runtime SIMD multiversioning and match-finder and loop changes. The output must stay a valid stream.

source_notes: Levers: runtime SIMD multiversioning, LLVM -enable-dfa-jump-thread flag recovering small-chunk performance, compression PRs by Brian Pane (not detailed on page). q:"about 6% at the default level of 6, and over 10% at the \"best compression\" level 9." Gains are single-digit percent so poor headroom; pair with a zlib 1.3 baseline for larger S (INFERRED, not on page). Output of deflate need not be byte-identical across impls, gate on inflate(roundtrip).
source_version: zlib-ng (version not stated on page; blog says only latest) as C reference; or earlier zlib-rs -> zlib-rs 0.4.2 (libz-rs-sys)

Band.why: No dated public evidence of agent outcomes on this work; with single-digit headroom a frontier agent likely lands near zero reward.

Build.why: Estimated 3-5 days; offline Rust vendoring and base selection unknown; smoke_build skipped.

Fit.why: CPU-only Rust; SIMD runtime detection should work under gVisor; noise is the risk, not kernel features.

Hor.why: 8h is plausible for several levers, but the gains are small and do not fill the tier.

Lic.why: Zlib licence permits shipping source, data and reference.

Multi.why: Levers (match finder, copy, CRC/adler, inflate loop) are separable, but partial credit is compressed into a few percent of speedup.

Nov.why: Highest L0 neighbours are internal seeds; the public neighbour is 0.105, below 0.15, and not crowded.

Real.why: Real upstream project with releases through v0.6.8 and a vendor blog; 0.4.2 confirmed via blog.

Ref.why: The reference speedup over any base is unmeasured; vendor numbers are vs zlib-ng, and the base tag was not found.

Seal.why: Reference is public in git history and later crates; closable only by a history-less snapshot of an unidentified base.

Surf.why: Roundtrip plus independent inflater over generated and corpus inputs is a few thousand checks at most, not an unlimited oracle.

spike_plan.kill_if: No earlier base tag can be found, or CV exceeds the gap, or the speedup is under 3%.
spike_plan.pass_if: Measured speedup of 0.4.2 over the chosen base is at least 5% with run-to-run CV below half that gap, and a base exists that is not the reference.
steps: In a throwaway networked Linux container, clone zlib-rs and check out the v0.4.2 tag; if absent, locate the 0.4.2 commit by its release date in the history.
Identify candidate earlier base tags/commits and record which one the seed's base would be.
Build libz-rs-sys offline-capable (vendor crates) and confirm it runs the inflate and deflate benchmarks.
Run deflate at levels 6 and 9 and inflate on 1 KB and 64 KB chunks: 20 runs each, base vs 0.4.2, record wall-clock medians.
Compute run-to-run coefficient of variation on the 8-core gVisor-like setup; compare to the expected 6-13% gap.
Check that roundtrip through an independent inflater passes on the same corpus.

v1.summary: The zlib-rs project, v0.4.2 and the Zlib licence check out, but the earlier base tag was not found and the published speedups are vs zlib-ng, so the reference's own gain over any base is unmeasured. Headroom is single-digit percent on wall-clock medians, which is too noisy to grade, so the seed is killed with K4 unless a base and a larger measured gap are found.
